claim:al20-34-novel-demonstration.statement: Route 3.4 demonstrations test and evaluate technologies, processes, methods or approaches new or unknown in the relevant LEADER area.
claim:al20-34-novel-demonstration.context: FUND-008 Annex I typology 3.4 definition; general route conditions still apply.
limitations: No local novelty, applicant eligibility or award is established for an actual project.

claim:al20-34-results-publication.statement: Information about the demonstration and its results must be published online and retained for at least three years after final payment.
claim:al20-34-results-publication.context: FUND-008 typology 3.4 publicity obligations; information starts with the activity and results are added as available.
limitations: The claim records the inspected edition, not current call availability.

claim:npl3-heritage-need.statement: NPL3 addresses conservation, enhancement and dissemination of the territory's natural and cultural rural heritage.
claim:npl3-heritage-need.context: FUND-013 section 4.3 prioritised needs addressable through LEADER; the strategy ranking is not a selection-point value.
limitations: An activity must actually address the need; linking it does not select a criterion or certify delivery.

claim:mr2-runoff-capture.statement: MR2 describes collecting suitable local runoff around scattered planting groups in dry landscapes.
claim:mr2-runoff-capture.context: FOREST-002 MR2/oasification discussion; receiving soil, terrain and safe overflow require site assessment.
limitations: Annual rainfall alone does not determine suitability, usable runoff or survival.

claim:mr2-preparation-depth.statement: The MR2 preparation discussion describes 60 x 60 x 60 cm holes; this preparation envelope does not specify root-collar burial depth.
claim:mr2-preparation-depth.context: FOREST-002 page 134 soil-preparation narrative; preparation geometry and plant installation depth are different measurements.
limitations: This is handbook guidance with site restrictions, not a generated excavation or planting prescription.

claim:mr2-stone-mulch.statement: The MR2 establishment discussion describes a microcatchment and stone mulch around the established plant.
claim:mr2-stone-mulch.context: FOREST-002 page 134; material-specific protective establishment context.
limitations: No material cost, irrigation saving or comparison with organic mulch is inferred.

claim:mr2-density-area-basis.statement: The MR2 discussion gives low whole-area tree densities below 100 stems/ha alongside approximately 6 x 6 m spacing within groups.
claim:mr2-density-area-basis.context: FOREST-002 page 132; whole landscape area and local grouped planting area must be distinguished.
limitations: These figures must not be treated as the same uniform hectare-wide grid or substituted for Designer assumptions.

claim:mr2-stock-narrative.statement: The MR2 narrative permits ordinary forestry stock above 200 cm3 and describes larger stock above 1000 cm3 as preferable.
claim:mr2-stock-narrative.context: FOREST-002 page 133 narrative on stock format; separate from the following summary table.
limitations: A qualified narrative preference; preserve its context alongside the table rather than choosing a stock default.

claim:mr2-stock-table.statement: The MR2 summary table lists one-year stock in 200-300 cm3 forestry containers.
claim:mr2-stock-table.context: FOREST-002 page 134 table 5.19; the table lists a smaller stock format than the narrative preference.
limitations: This source tension is unresolved; the table does not silently override the narrative.

claim:designer-carob-density-assumption.statement: The current Designer starts carob from an illustrative project density assumption.
claim:designer-carob-density-assumption.context: Current repository default, resolved from the central rule bundle on each query; saved designs may retain different bundles.
limitations: No numerical default is copied into this claim and no handbook optimum is implied.

claim:designer-mr2-layout-assumption.statement: The Designer's exact MR2 drawing geometry is an illustrative project assumption.
claim:designer-mr2-layout-assumption.context: Current centres and donor/island/overflow drawing parameters are resolved from the central rule bundle.
limitations: Coordinates are not engineered catchment dimensions, treatment effects or permitted earthworks.

claim:mr2-establishment-water-gap.statement: The inspected Mojacar and Nijar case passages do not document original seedling establishment-water volumes.
claim:mr2-establishment-water-gap.context: Bounded to FOREST-002 pages 135-137 and the existing MR2 reference context; Nijar includes a naturalised population.
limitations: This is not a literature-wide absence claim, a verified zero-water seedling protocol or an inferred irrigation dose.

claim:life-nature-objectives.statement: The LIFE Nature and Biodiversity sub-programme supports nature and biodiversity objectives through innovative approaches, best practices, governance and replication, including protection, maintenance and restoration of natural capital.
claim:life-nature-objectives.context: The 2025-2027 work programme describes programme objectives and priority areas; it is not a project-specific eligibility decision.
limitations: A restoration theme alone does not establish an eligible project, applicant or available call.

claim:life-sap-purpose.statement: Standard Action Projects are a distinct LIFE grant format supporting innovative approaches, best practices, policy implementation and the wider deployment of successful solutions.
claim:life-sap-purpose.context: Section 4.1.1 of the 2025-2027 work programme. Strategic projects, technical assistance and other actions are separate formats.
limitations: This is a framework description, not a claim that every Nature project or catalogue route is a Standard Action Project.

claim:life-sap-cofinancing-framework.statement: The 2025-2027 Standard Action Project framework generally limits cofinancing to 60% of eligible costs. Nature and Biodiversity projects may reach 75% only under its qualifying habitat/species conditions, exclusive targeting and proposal justification requirements.
claim:life-sap-cofinancing-framework.context: Section 4.1.1.1 spans PDF pages 20-21. Read the complete qualifying categories and requirement that all actions benefit the qualifying habitats or species.
limitations: These are conditional framework ceilings, not an award rate, financing input or automatic qualification.
The exact applicable call, eligible costs, habitat/species status and supporting evidence require their own review. No current call is assessed.

claim:kermes-climate-context.statement: The factsheet describes a broad climatic range for kermes oak, including occurrence around 200 mm annual rainfall at Cabo de Gata, while reporting 400-800 mm as its more favourable rainfall context.
claim:kermes-climate-context.context: FOREST-003 climate discussion on PDF page 2; natural occurrence and established vegetation, not an establishment trial.
limitations: The rainfall figures are not a seedling-survival threshold, irrigation prescription or parcel-suitability rule.
Local soil, exposure, provenance and establishment conditions still require assessment.

claim:kermes-soil-context.statement: The factsheet reports kermes oak on dry, stony ground, commonly calcareous, while also describing acidic substrates and a range of soil types.
claim:kermes-soil-context.context: Distribution and substrate descriptions on PDF pages 1-2.
limitations: Broad occurrence does not demonstrate adequate rootable volume, water availability or performance at a proposed planting point.

claim:kermes-community-context.statement: The factsheet lists kermes oak with thermophilous vegetation including carob, lentisk, palmetto and wild olive, among other community contexts.
claim:kermes-community-context.context: Vegetation discussion on FOREST-003 PDF page 2; descriptive community occurrence.
limitations: Co-occurrence does not establish a mandatory planting mixture, planting distance or beneath-crown compatibility.
Existing Designer species choices and placement rules remain separately owned project assumptions.

claim:kermes-coscoja-series.statement: The factsheet lists a semi-arid Quercus coccifera vegetation series under the Latin name Rhamno lycioidis-Querceto cocciferae sigmetum.
claim:kermes-coscoja-series.context: One vegetation-series entry on FOREST-003 PDF page 3, distinct from the warm-series naming tension.
limitations: The source list is not a complete planting recipe. Its climatic terminology must not be used to classify a parcel automatically.

claim:kermes-warm-series-vernacular.statement: The warm thermo-mesomediterranean series entry is described in the factsheet prose as a coscoja or Quercus coccifera series.
claim:kermes-warm-series-vernacular.context: The two descriptions refer to the same warm-series entry on FOREST-003 PDF page 3; they remain unresolved together.
limitations: Retain the source description alongside its different Latin label. No corrected series identity is selected.

claim:kermes-warm-series-latin.statement: That same warm-series entry gives the parenthesized Latin label Bupleuro gibraltarii-Pistacieto lentisci, naming lentisk rather than repeating the prose Quercus label.
claim:kermes-warm-series-latin.context: The two descriptions refer to the same warm-series entry on FOREST-003 PDF page 3; they remain unresolved together.
limitations: The retained Designer display label is an existing interpretation, not a resolution of this source tension. Further vegetation-taxonomy review is required.

claim:drone-irrigator-R1.statement: Growboxx and Waterboxx datasheets document refill access; Cocoon field guidance describes subsequent watering and a possible refill-hole adaptation. These are different products and materials.
claim:drone-irrigator-R1.context: Bounded Drone Irrigator review, 4 November 2026. Source findings, author assumptions and integration readiness remain distinct.
limitations: Not an operational preset, universal species prescription or verified autonomous watering product.

claim:drone-irrigator-R2.statement: The NIEBLAS manual records a historical EUR 7.8 Cocoon purchase cost, not a current delivered bulk quote. Current biodegradable reservoir procurement and installed lifecycle cost remain unresolved in this reviewed evidence.
claim:drone-irrigator-R2.context: Bounded Drone Irrigator review, 4 November 2026. Source findings, author assumptions and integration readiness remain distinct.
limitations: Not an operational preset, universal species prescription or verified autonomous watering product.

claim:drone-irrigator-R3.statement: Carob has Cocoon field-use evidence with poor performance at a harsh late-spring Jordan site; cork oak has Cocoon field-use evidence in Portugal. Neither establishes local suitability or a universal water requirement.
claim:drone-irrigator-R3.context: Bounded Drone Irrigator review, 4 November 2026. Source findings, author assumptions and integration readiness remain distinct.
limitations: Not an operational preset, universal species prescription or verified autonomous watering product.

claim:drone-irrigator-R4.statement: Reviewed reservoir release claims, trial applied water and mixed-species water-use totals do not establish daily supplemental-demand profiles for the app catalogue at the intended site and establishment stage.
claim:drone-irrigator-R4.context: Bounded Drone Irrigator review, 4 November 2026. Source findings, author assumptions and integration readiness remain distinct.
limitations: Not an operational preset, universal species prescription or verified autonomous watering product.

claim:drone-irrigator-R5.statement: The existing MR2 handbook passages and Cocoon installation guidance are context for preparing cluster choices. They do not validate drone rotor/hose clearance or an automatically suitable mixture.
claim:drone-irrigator-R5.context: Bounded Drone Irrigator review, 4 November 2026. Source findings, author assumptions and integration readiness remain distinct.
limitations: Not an operational preset, universal species prescription or verified autonomous watering product.

issue:mr2-stock-source-tension.explanation: The narrative prefers larger stock while table 5.19 lists smaller stock. Preserve both qualified contexts; neither is automatically adopted.
limitations: This is a source tension, not proof that the two passages are logically incompatible.

issue:mr2-water-evidence-gap.explanation: Original seedling establishment-water volumes are not documented in the selected case passages.
limitations: Absence is bounded to the inspected passages and does not imply zero irrigation.

issue:kermes-warm-series-naming.explanation: The warm-series line uses coscoja/Quercus coccifera in prose and Bupleuro-Pistacieto lentisci in its Latin label. Preserve both descriptions pending vegetation-series review; select neither as a corrected source identity.
limitations: Bounded to the inspected line and existing research context. This does not invalidate every vegetation-series entry in the factsheet.
Retained Designer series labels and mixtures are unchanged.

issue:drone-irrigator-capacities.explanation: Different reviewed editions describe 20 L and approximately 25 L. Select the actual supplied product and measure usable fill; do not average or silently select.
limitations: No operational value or rule is selected by publishing this issue.

issue:drone-irrigator-refill-regimes.explanation: Initial single-fill concept and supplemental summer-refill practice coexist. This is a regimen/engineering tension, not proof that all Cocoons are refillable or unsuitable.
limitations: No operational value or rule is selected by publishing this issue.

issue:drone-irrigator-planting-depth.explanation: Installation wording differs in context. Retain both passages for nursery/site review; do not encode a root-collar-depth rule from this research.
limitations: No operational value or rule is selected by publishing this issue.
